FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Inorganic Chemicals Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 


This standard was originally published in 1962 and first revised in 1980. During its last revision, the relevance 
of impurities (that is, sulphates, total sulphates, phosphates, chlorides, nitrates and aluminium) prescribed 
in the older version of this standard (that is, IS 2080 : 1962) was considered not significant in view of latest 
manufacturing technology introduced in the industry. Consequently, requirements for those characteristics have 
been deleted and new requirements were added for “residue on ignition, lead and arsenic”. Further, provision 
of additional requirements also incorporated to address the specific needs of chemical, electronics, paper and 
cosmetic industries and new grade of product also included. 


This standard is being revised again with the aim of updating the standard and also to take into consideration 
the technical advancements that have taken place since the publication of this standard. Also, methods of test for 
determination of strength by densitymeter and heavy metals by ICP have been incorporated. 


Hydrogen peroxide is mainly used as an oxidizing and bleaching agent in industry and also as disinfectant. Over 
the years the pattern of use has undergone a change and hydrogen peroxide is now increasingly used by other 
industries, namely, chemicals, electronics, paper, textile, cosmetics, etc. 


The composition of Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given at Annex E. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

STABILIZED HYDROGEN 
PEROXIDE — SPECIFICATION

1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements, the methods 
of sampling and test for stabilized hydrogen peroxide. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given below contain provisions, which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreement based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below:

arsenic

randomization procedures 
(first revision) 
3 GRADES 


The material shall be of six grades as follows: 
a) Grade 1 of nominal strength 70.0 percent by mass, 
b) Grade 2 of nominal strength 60.0 percent by mass, 
c) Grade 3 of nominal strength 50.0 percent by mass, 
d) Grade 4 of nominal strength 35.0 percent by mass, 


e) Grade 5 of nominal strength 6.0 percent by mass, 
and 


f) Grade 6 of nominal strength 3.0 percent by mass. 


4 REQUIREMENTS 


4.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of clear, colourless 
liquid, free from suspended impurities and dust 
particles. 


4.2 Strength 


The strength of the material, when tested according to 
the method prescribed in Annex A or alternate method 
C-9, shall on the date of packing, be not less than 
70.0 percent (m/m) for Grade 1, 60.0 percent (m/m) for 
Grade 2, 50.0 percent (m/m) for Grade 3, 35.0 percent 
(m/m) for Grade 4, 6.0 percent (m/m) for Grade 5 and 
3.0 percent (m/m) for Grade 6. 


4.2.1 This requirement shall also be met when the 
material has been stored and handled as prescribed in 
5.1. 


4.3 Stability 
4.3.1 For Grades 1 


The material, when tested as prescribed in Annex B, 
shall not evolve more than 0.3 ml of oxygen per minute 
per 25 ml at 75 °C. 


4.3.2 For Grades 2,3 and 4 


The material, when tested as prescribed in Annex B, 
shall not evolve more than 0.3 ml of oxygen per minute 
per 25 ml at 100 °C. 


4.3.3 For Grades 5 and 6 


The material when tested as prescribed in Annex B, 
shall not lose its strength by more than 4 percent by 
mass of its original strength. 


4.4 The material shall also comply with the requirements 
given in Table 1. 


4.5 Additional Requirements 


Additional requirements for specific uses, if required, 
may be prescribed as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the supplier.

5 PACKING AND MARKING 


5.1 Packing 


5.1.1 All containers in which the material is packed 
shall be clean and dry. 


5.1.2 The material shall be packed in bottles or carboys 
except Grade 1 as agreed to between the purchaser 
and the supplier. The material of construction of the 
container shall be compatible with the properties of 
hydrogen peroxide. Where the material of construction 
is glass, the bottles shall be made of neutral glass or 
carboys made of HDPE/HM-HDPE (Virgin material). 
Grade 1,2,3 and 4 shall also be supplied in bulk tankers 
where the material of construction is SS 316L or SS 
304L with mirror finish surface (minimum of 320 grit 
finish). 


5.1.2.1 Containers may be of valve or vent type closure 
or without it. For containers with valve or vent type 
closure arrangement, the minimum ullage should be 
10 percent. For containers without valve or vent type 
closure, the ullage space shall be not less than one half 
of the total capacity of the container for Grades 2, 3 and 
4 and not less than one-fourth of the total capacity of the 
container for Grades 5 and 6. For Grades 1 and 2, the 
maximum capacity of the containers should be 2 litres, 
when hermetically sealed. For Grade 1, the material 
is only supplied in tanker with proper venting system 
and proper sealing to avoid any pilferages during 
transportation. Grade 2, 3 and 4 are normally supplied 
in dedicated tankers or packed in barrels and carboys 
wherein proper vents and seal ring are provided on the 
caps. Grade 5 and 6 when packed in containers without 
valve or vent. 


5.1.3 In the packaging of glass containers, suitable 
cushioning material shall be used. 


5.1.4 All the containers shall be securely closed. 


5.1.5 The containers shall be stored away from direct 
sunlight, preferably in the dark. 


5.1.6 The containers shall be stored and handled as 
directed by the manufacturer to ensure stability. 


5.2 Marking 
The containers shall bear legibly and indelibly the 
following information: 

a) Name and grade of the material: 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer and his 

recognized trade-mark, if any; 

c) Quantity of the material in litres or in Kgs/MT; 

d) Month and year of packing, 

e) Batch number, and 

f) Storage instructions with Safety pictograms. 


5.2.1 Containers shall also prominently display the 
words ‘CORROSIVE, HANDLE WITH CARE’ and 
the appropriate symbol for labelling of dangerous 
goods prescribed in IS 1260 (Part 1). 


5.2.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the products 
may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


6 SAMPLING 


The method of drawing representative samples of the 
material, number of tests to be performed and the criteria 
for conformity of the material to the requirements of 
this specification shall be as prescribed in Annex D. 


15 2080 : 2021

ANNEX A 
( Clauses 4.2 and 7.1) 
DETERMINATION OF STRENGTH 


A-1 REAGENTS 


A-1.1 Dilute Sulphuric Acid, 10 percent (v/v). 


A-1.2 Standard Potassium Permanganate Solution, 
0.5 N and 0.1 N. 


A-2 PROCEDURE 


A-2.1 For Grades 1,2,3 and 4 


Weigh accurately about 1 g of the material in a 5 ml 
capacity weighing bottle. Measure about 100 ml of 
dilute sulphuric acid into a 500 ml conical beaker 
(philips conical beaker with spout). Add potassium 
permanganate solution (0.1 N) dropwise until mixture 
persists with a faint permanent pink colour. Transfer the 
weighing bottle with the material carefully to the beaker 
and titrate with potassium permanganate solution 
(0.5 N) to the appearance of the same faint permanent 
pink colour, obtained before the addition of the sample. 


Recommended weight of the sample (W g) 


Grade 1 — 70% w/w HP 
Grade 2 — 60% w/w HP 
Grade 3 — 50% w/w HP 
Grade 4 — 35% w/w HP 


0.4 to 0.5 g sample 


0.5 to 0.6 g sample 
0.6 to 0.7 g sample 


0.9 to 1.0 g sample 


A-2.2 For Grades 5 and 6 


Weigh accurately about | g of the material into a 5 ml 
capacity weighing bottle. Measure about 100 ml of 
dilute sulphuric acid into a 500 m1 conical beaker. Add 
potassium permanganate solution (0.1 N) dropwise 
until the mixture persists with a faint pink colour. 
Transfer the weighing bottle with the material carefully 
to the beaker and titrate with potassium permanganate 
solution (0.1 N) to the appearance of the same faint 
permanent pink colour obtained before the addition of 
the material. 


A-2.3 Calculation 


Hydrogen peroxide, percent by mass = 


1.7008 x Vx N 
M 
where, 

V= volume in ml, of standard potassium 
permanganate solution consumed in the 
titration; 

N= normality of standard potassium permanganate 
solution; and 

M = mass in g, of the material taken for the test. 


A-2.4 Alternate Method 


Determination of strength by Densitymeter as 
prescribed at C-9. 


15 2080 : 2021 


ANNEX B 
( Clauses 4.3.1, 4.3.2 and 4.3.3 ) 
DETERMINATION OF STABILITY 


WARNING 


It is essential that hydrogen peroxide be handled and 
stored so as to avoid the risk of violent decomposition 
or explosion. In particular only clean equipment 
compatible with the product should be used (for 
example, glass or unplasticized polyvinyl chloride) 
and containers should be vented to prevent build-up 
of pressure. Contact with all combustible substances 
should be avoided. 


It is essential that personnel handling hydrogen 
peroxide be familiar with the detailed advice contained 
in the supplier’s material safety data sheet, and be 
provided with protection against splashes in the eye 
and on the skin. 


It is essential that eye protection be worn during the 
operation of this method. 


B-1 FOR GRADES 1,2,3 AND 4 


B-1.1 Apparatus 


B-1.1.1 Boiling Water-Bath (for Grade 1, the bath 
temperature is controlled at 75 °C) 


B-1.1.2 Reaction Tube, of size 150 x 25 mm with 
ground-glass cone. 


B-1.1.3 Liebig Condenser, effective length 75 mm, 
ground-glass socket. 


B-1.1.4 Gas Burette, with side arm and tap, 25 ml 
capacity with graduation of 0.1 ml. 


B-1.1.5 Levelling Tube, a little longer than the gas 
burette. 


B-1.1.6 Pipette, one mark with safety bulb, 25 ml 
capacity. 


B-1.1.7 Complete assembly of the apparatus is shown 
in Fig. 1. 


All dimension as in millimetres 


FIG. | APPARATUS FOR DETERMINATION OF STABILITY OF HYDROGEN PEROXIDE (GASOMETRIC METHOD) 


15 2080 : 2021 


NOTE — All glass apparatus coming in contact with hydrogen 

peroxide should be: 

a) of borosilicate glass, 

b) conditioned with nitric acid (relative density 1.42) at 
100 °C for 30 minutes and then rinsed well with water 
before its commissioning, 

c) stored in dust free atmosphere, and 

d) well rinsed and conditioned with hydrogen peroxide before 
use. 


B-1.2 Procedure 


Pipette 25.0 ml of the sample into reaction tube and 
place the tube in continuously boiling and constant level 
water bath (for Grade 1, the temperature of the Water 
bath is controlled at 75 °C). Connect the condenser 
and open tap A. Allow 10 min for the condenser and 
reaction tube to equilibrate and adjust the water level in 
the gas burette to the zero mark by dropwise addition 
of water to the levelling tube. Close tap A and start 
the stop watch. Periodically equalize the water levels 
in the gas burette and the levelling tube by carefully 
and gradually draining water from tap B. Continue for 
20 mins and stop the watch. Accurately equalize the 
water levels in the gas burette and the levelling tube in 
the manner described above and measure the volume 
of oxygen evolved. Note the duration of the test as T 
minutes. 

NOTE — Separate reaction tubes should be used for each 

grade of hydrogen peroxide. Care should be taken never to 


allow the reaction tube to become completely dry during the 
course of testing. 


B-1.3 Calculation 


Stability of the sample, ml of oxygen/min/25 ml = is 


T 
where 


V= volume in ml, of oxygen evolved; and 
T- duration of the test in minutes. 


B-2 FOR GRADES 5 AND 6 


B-2.1 Apparatus 


B-2.1.1 Round Bottom Flask, of 250 ml capacity, fitted 
with a socket to fit in the reflux condenser (see B-2.1.2) 
and having a long neck. If new, the flask shall be 


pre-treated by boiling in it 100 ml of hydrogen peroxide 
(of the same strength as it is intended to test) under 
reflux for 30 min. It shall then be cleaned and kept 
exclusively for this test. Between tests, it shall be 
cleaned with nitric acid and rinsed thoroughly with 
water. 


B-2.1.2 Reflux Condenser, double surface, fitted with a 
cone to fit in the round-bottom flask (see B-2.1.1) and 
with an effective length of 15 to 20 cm. 


B-2.1.3 Preparation of Apparatus 


Wash the condenser with water, cover the top with a 
clean dust proof cap, for example, tube or beaker or 
other vessel of suitable size and allow to drain. Wash 
the flask with water and allow to drain. Draw about 
50 ml of the material through a 100 ml pipette and rinse 
the pipette thoroughly, transfer to the round-bottom 
flask to wash the flask and reject the washings. 


B-2.2 Procedure 


Pipette 100 ml of the material into the round-bottom 
flask and attach the condenser to the flask. Reflux 
gently on a sand-bath or electric heating mantle 
for exactly three hours, timing this period from the 
commencement of boiling. Cover the flask with a paper 
cap and cool rapidly under running water. During 
all these operations, care shall be taken to avoid 
any contamination with dust. When the solution has 
cooled, determine its strength according to the method 
prescribed in Annex A. 


B-3 CALCULATION 
B-3.1 Stability, percent loss in strength = 


A-B 
100 x‘ 


where 
A= strength of the original material as obtained 
following the procedure prescribed in A-2; and 


B= strength of the boiled material as obtained 
following the procedure prescribed in B-2.2. 


15 2080 : 2021 


ANNEX C 
( Clause 4.4, Table 1) 
METHODS OF TEST FOR STABILIZED HYDROGEN PEROXIDE 


C-1 ACIDITY 

C-1.1 Reagents 

C-1.1.1 Standard Sodium Hydroxide Solution, 0.1 N. 
C-1.1.2 Rectified Spirit — see IS 323. 


C-1.1.3 Screened Methyl Red Indicator, weigh 0.050 g 
of methylene blue in a 100m1 beaker and dissolve in 
50 ml of rectified spirit. Weigh 0.10 g of methyl red into 
a 100 m1 beaker and dissolve in 50 ml of rectified spirit, 
by gently warming, if required. Mix the two solutions 
and store in an amber bottle. The solution should not be 
used for more than three months. 


C-1.2 Procedure 


Pipette out 100 ml of the material into a 400 ml beaker 
containing 100 ml of carbon dioxide-free distilled 
water (freshly boiled), add a few drops of screened 
methyl red indicator and titrate with standard sodium 
hydroxide solution till the colour changes to green. 


C-1.3 Calculation 
Acidity (as H,SO,), g/100 ml = 0.0490 x VN 


where 


V= volume in ml, of standard sodium hydroxide 
solution; and 
N= normality of standard sodium hydroxide 


solution. 


C-2 DETERMINATION OF RESIDUE ON 
EVAPORATION 


C-2.1 Procedure 


Evaporate 25 ml of the material to dryness in a 
pre-weighed, dry platinum dish on a boiling water-bath 
with controlled decomposition by addition of distilled 
water. Dry the residue to constant mass in an oven 
maintained at a temperature of 105 + 2 °C. Preserve the 
dish with contents for test in C-3. 


C-2.2 Calculation 
Residue on evaporation, g/100 ml =4 (B— A) 
where 
B= mass in g, of the dish after drying; and 
A= mass in g, of the empty dish. 


C-3 DETERMINATION OF RESIDUE ON 
IGNITION 


C-3.1 Procedure 
Gently ignite the residue obtained in C-2.1 in a furnace 
(800 °C). Cool and weigh till constant mass is obtained. 
Preserve the dish with contents for Trace metals test as 
prescribed in C-8. 
C-3.2 Calculation 
Residue on ignition, g/100 ml = 4 (B — A) 
where 

B= mass in g, of the dish after ignition; and 

A= mass in g, of the empty dish. 


C-4IRON 
C-4.1 Apparatus 


C-4.1.1 Nessler 
(see IS 4161). 


Cylinders, 50 ml capacity 


C-4.2 Reagents 


C-4.2.1 Citric Acid Solution, approximately 10 percent 
(w/). 


C-4.2.2 Thioglycollic Acid 
C-4.2.3 Ammonium Hydroxide, | : 4 (v/v) (approx). 


C-4.2.4 Standard Iron Solution, dissolve 1.404 g of 
ferrous ammonium sulphate [FeSO, (NH,), SO,.6H,0] 
in about 100 ml of water containing 10 ml of dilute 
sulphuric acid (10 percent v/v). Dilute to 1 000 ml. Take 
50 ml of this solution in a 1 000 ml graduated flask 
and dilute again to mark. One millilitre of this diluted 
solution contains 0.01 mg of iron (as Fe). This diluted 
solution shall be freshly prepared before performing 
the test. 


C-4.3 Procedure 


C-4.3.1 Preparation of Solution 


Take 50 ml of the material into a beaker and add 
5 ml of sodium hydroxide solution. Commence the 
decomposition by slight heating. When decomposition is 
complete and the material is free of active oxygen, cool. 
Dilute the cooled solution quantitatively to 100 ml. 


15 2080 : 2021 


C-4.3.2 Take 20 ml of the solution as prepared in 
C-4.3.1. Add 3 ml of citric acid solution and 5 drops of 
thioglycollic acid, mix and then add 10 ml ofammoniun 
hydroxide. Allow to stand for 5 min. Transfer the 
solution to a Nessler cylinder and dilute to 50 ml. Carry 
out a control test using | ml of standard iron solution 
by the same steps as for test sample. Transfer to 
another Nessler cylinder and dilute to the same volume. 
Compare the intensity of colour produced in the two 
cylinders. 


C-4.3.3 The limit prescribed in Table 1 shall be taken 
as not having been exceeded if the intensity of colour 
produced by the sample, is not greater than that 
produced in the control test. 


C-4.4 Alternate Method 


Alternately, Iron content can also be determined by 
ICP-OES method as prescribed at C-8. 


C-5 COPPER 


C-5.1 Apparatus 


C-5.1.1 Nessler 
(see IS 4161). 


Cylinders, 50 ml capacity 


C-5.2 Reagents 


C-5.2.1 Sodium Hydroxide Solution, approximately 
0.5 .N. 


C-5.2.2 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid, approximately 
0.5N. 


C-5.2.3 Citric Acid Solution, approximately 10 percent 
(w/). 


C-5.2.4 Sodium Diethyldithiocarbamate Solution, 
Dissolve 0.1 g of sodium diethyldithiocarbamate in 
100 ml of copper-free water. Filter, if necessary. 
Preserve in an amber colour glass bottle and store in a 
dark place. This solution should not be used after two 
weeks. 


C-5.2.5 Ammonium Hydroxide, approximately 1 : 4 
WA). 


C-5.2.6 Standard Copper Solution, dissolve 0.392 8 g 
of copper sulphate pentahydrate (CuSO,.5H,0) in 
1 000 ml of copper-free water. Pipette out 10 ml of this 
solution and dilute to 1 000 ml. One millilitre of the 
diluted solution contains 0.001 mg of copper (as Cu). 
The diluted solution should be freshly prepared before 
use. 


NOTE — The purity of the salt should be checked before use. 
C-5.2.7 Extraction Solvent, two alternative extraction 


solvents, amyl alcohol and carbon tetrachloride, are 
prescribed. It is permitted to use any one of them. 


C-5.3 Procedure 


Take 100 ml of the material in a beaker and add 
10 ml of sodium hydroxide solution. Heat gently 
until decomposition is complete and then add 10 ml 
of dilute hydrochloric acid. Heat the solution under 
constant stirring for about 5 min. Cool and add 
2.5 ml of citric acid solution. Neutralize the excess acid 
with ammonium hydroxide and add 10 ml in excess, 
followed by 10 ml of sodium diethyldithiocarbamate 
solution. Transfer the solution to a separating funnel, 
stir and allow to stand for 5 min. Extract the yellow 
colour produced, with 10 ml of the extraction solvent. 
Repeat the extraction procedure further twice using 
5 ml of the extraction solvent. Collect non-aqueous 
layers together, centrifuge to remove cloudiness. 
Alternatively, dry with anhydrous sodium sulphate. 
Make up the volume to 25 ml with fresh clear extracting 
solvent. Carry out a control test using 10 ml of standard 
copper solution, proceeding exactly as for the material 
under test. Compare the intensity of the colour produced 
in the two cylinders. 


C-5.3.1 The limits laid down in Table 1 shall be 
taken as not having been exceeded if the intensity of 
colour produced by the sample is not greater than that 
produced in the control test. 


C-5.4 Alternate Method 


Alternately, Copper content can also be determined by 
ICP-OES method as prescribed at C-8. 


C-6 LEAD 


C-6.1 Apparatus 


C-6.1.1 Nessler 
(see IS 4161). 


Cylinders, 50 ml capacity 


C-6.2 Reagents 

C-6.2.1 Sodium Carbonate, solid. 

C-6.2.2 Dilute Nitric Acid, 1 : 3 (v/v). 

C-6.2.3 Dilute Ammonium Hydroxide, 1 : 2 (v/v). 


C-6.2.4 Standard Lead Solution, dissolve 1.598 g of 
lead nitrate (pre-dried for one hour at 100 °C and cooled 
in a desiccator) in about 200 ml of water. Transfer it to 
a 1 000 ml volumetric flask, add 50 ml of concentrated 
nitric acid and dilute to the mark with water. Mix well. 
Store in polyethylene bottle. One millilitre of this 
solution is equivalent to 1 000 ug of lead (Pb). This 
solution shall not be used for more than two weeks. 


C-6.2.4.1 Diluted standard lead solution , dilute 
1.0 ml of standard lead solution (C-6.2.4) to 100 ml 
in a volumetric flask. One millilitre of this solution is 
equivalent to 10 lug of lead (Pb). The diluted solution 
shall be prepared afresh each time. 


C-6.2.5 Glacial Acetic Acid, see IS 695. 


C-6.2.6 Hydrogen Sulphide Gas or Sodium Sulphide 
Solution, 1 percent (m/v). 


C-6.3 Procedure 


C-6.3.1 Evaporate 50 ml of hydrogen peroxide, 40 ml 
of water and 0.1 g of sodium carbonate to dryness in a 
suitable size silica dish on a steam/water-bath. Rinse 
the dish from sides towards centre with about 10 ml 
of water and again evaporate to dryness. Dissolve the 
residue in water and transfer quantitatively to 50 ml 
volumetric flask and make up the volume. 


C-6.3.2 Transfer 2 ml of the solution to a 50 m1 Nessler 
cylinder and add 1 ml of dilute nitric acid and about 
30 ml of water followed by 5 ml of dilute ammonium 
hydroxide. Make up the volume to 50 ml. Mix well. 


C-6.3.3 Pipette out 2 ml of freshly prepared diluted 
standard lead solution into a second Nessler cylinder. 
Add 1 ml of glacial acetic acid, 30 ml of water and 
10 ml of dilute ammonium hydroxide. Make up the 
volume to 50 ml with water. Mix well. 


C-6.3.4 Pass hydrogen sulphide gas through the control 
and the sample solution at the rate of 2-3 bubbles 
per second, for 1 min. Alternatively, 5 ml of sodium 
sulphide solution may be used in place of hydrogen 
sulphide gas. After 5 min compare the colour developed 
by the two solutions. 


C-6.3.5 The limits prescribed in Table 1 shall be 
considered to have not been exceeded if the colour 
produced by the sample is not greater than in the 
control test. 


C-6.4 Alternate Method 


Alternately, Lead content can also be determined by 
ICP-OES method as prescribed at C-8. 


C-7 ARSENIC 


C-7.1 Procedure 


Take 5 ml of the sample solution (prepared as in 
C-6.3.1), mix with 15 ml of water and 10 ml of 
concentrated hydrochloric acid. Determine the arsenic 
by the modified Gutzeit method prescribed in 5.1 of 
IS 2088, using of comparison of a stain obtained for 
the sample with 0.01 mg of arsenic trioxide (as As,O,). 


C-7.2 Alternate Method 


Alternately, Arsenic content can also be determined by 
ICP-OES method as prescribed at C-8. 


IS 2080 : 2021 


C-8 DETERMINATION OF TRACE 
METALS-IRON, COPPER, LEAD AND 
ARSENIC 

C-8.1 Instrument 

C-8.1.1 Inductively Coupled Plasma - Optical 


Emission Spectrometer (Integrated with Computer 
Operated Software) 


C-8.2 Trace Metals to be Analyzed: Fe, Cu, Pb and As 


Wave length for each element used: 


Element Wave length Viewing 
(nm) mode 
Fe 238.204 Axial 
Cu 327.393 Axial 
Pb 220.353 Axial 
As 193.696 Axial 


NOTE— These wave length may vary from instrument 
to instrument and conditions used. Hence, wavelength for 
particular element should be determined during developing 
method in the instrument. 


C-8.3 Sample Preparation 


50 ml sample of stabilized hydrogen peroxide taken 
in a 100 ml evaporating dish, put a platinum piece of 
1 cm x 1 cm in it. Place the evaporating dish three 
quarters immersed in a water bath initially kept at 
room temperature. Start heating, decomposition 
is observed. Maintain heating to control rate of 
decomposition. When decomposition is complete, 
gently evaporate the solution in dish to dryness. 
Dissolve the content remained in the evaporating dish 
in ultrapure demineralised water and add 2-3 drops of 
ultrapure nitric acid, make up the volume to 100 ml in 
a volumetric flask. 


Alternately, the residue on ignition obtained as 
prescribed in C-3.1 is dissolved in 2 ml of ultrapure 
nitric acid with 2 ml of ultrapure distilled water. Make 
up the volume with of ultrapure dilute 5 percent nitric 
acid to 50 ml in a volumetric flask. 


C-8.4 Analysis on ICP 


C-8.4.1 Operation of the Instrument 


Set the instrument ready as per standard operating 
procedure prescribed in the manual of instrument 
supplier. 


Typical instrument operating condition for a specific 
model of equipment for information reference 
(see Note): 


15 2080 : 2021 


Parameter Setting 

PF powder 1300 W 

Nebulizer flow 0.8 L/min. 

Auxiliary flow 0.2 L/min. 

Plasma flow 15 L/min. 

Sample flow 1.5 ML/min 

Background correction Manual selection of points 
Measuring processing mode Peak area /Ht 

Read delay 60 

Replicates 3 


NOTE — Operating conditions may vary depending upon 
model, make, conditions etc. Hence, each laboratory should 
set its own operating conditions while developing method in 
the instrument. 


C-8.4.2 Drawing of Curves 
C-8.4.3 Preparation of Calibration Standards 


Two multi. element standards containing 
100 micrograms/l and 200 micrograms/l of Al, As, Ca, 
Cd, Co, Cr, Cu, Fe, Mg, Mn, Ni, Pb and Ni are prepared 
from 100 mg/l multi element standard in ultrapure 
demineralised water. 


C-8.4.4 Drawing of Standard Curves 


C-8.4.4.1 The hardware is set up properly as per 
manual. 


C-8.4.4.2 Introduce blank solution (ultrapure 
demineralised water) to the plasma, and then introduce 
Standard I (100 microgram/l) and standard II 
(200 microgram/l) to complete calibration of the 
instrument. 


C-8.4.4.3 Linear calibration curves is drawn through 
the blank and standards (I and II) are obtained for 
each element (with reference to their respective wave 
length). 


C-8.5 Determination of Trace Elements 


Sample as prepared above is introduced into the plasma 
and the concentration of each trace element determined 
by using external standards method with the help of 
calibration curve for respective elements at required 
wavelength. Read the concentration of the particular 
elements (say C) in microgram/| directly from the 


graph. 


10 


C-8.5.1 Calculation: 


Microgram/l of metal in H,O, = 


E final volume after evaporation 
x 


Sample volume 


=Cx or C x dilution factor 
NOTE 
1 100 here is final volume after evaporation 
2 50 is sample volume taken for evaporation 
3 Dilution factor here is 2. (100 + 50 = 2) 


4 Results can also be read directly on the instrument after 
adding appropriate dilution factor. 


C-9 DETERMINATION 
DENSITYMETER 


OF STRENGTH BY 


C-9.1 Instrument 
C-9.1.1 Densitymeter, fitted with autosampler. 
C-9.2 Analysis on the Instrument 


C-9.2.1 Calibration 


Standard hydrogen peroxide solution of various 
strength are analysed on the densitymeter at the standard 
temperature and a calibration graph is generated against 
which the sample is analysed. 


Performance checks of the instrument is carried 
out with air and ultra-pure water at the measuring 
temperature. This ensures the density and concentration 
measurements are highly consistent and the results are 
of highly repeatable accuracy. 


C-9.2.2 Analysis 
Select the calibration method. Place the sample tube 
into the sample bottle and press start. The instrument 


will flush the sample and start the analysis after the 
sampling is done. 

Ensure that there is no error message due to any air 
bubble. 

The screen shall display the strength of the sample, 
density and the temperature of the measurement. 

C-9.3 Result 

Strength of H202 = “A” where “A” is the reading of 
strength on the instrument. 


NOTE — Refer the manual of the Densitymeter for the 
calibration. 


15 2080 : 2021 


ANNEX D 
( Clause 6 ) 
SAMPLING OF STABILIZED HYDROGEN PEROXIDE 


D-1 SCALE OF SAMPLING 


D-1.1 Lot 


All the containers in a single consignment of the 
material of the same grade and drawn from a single 
batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If the 
consignment is found to consist of different batches 
of packing, the containers belonging to the same batch 
shall be grouped together and each such group shall 
constitute a separate lot. 


D-1.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the material in 
the lot to the requirements of the specification, samples 
shall be tested separately from each lot. The number 
of containers to be selected at random from the lot 
shall depend upon the size of the lot and shall be in 
accordance with Table 2. 


Table 2 Number of Containers to be Selected 
( Clause D-1.2 ) 


SI No. No. of Containers in The Lot Sample Size 

(N) (n) 
(D (2) (3) 
i) Up to 50 5 
ii) 51 to 100 7 
iii) 101 to 300 10 
iv) 301 to 1 000 15 
v) 1 001 and above 20 


D-1.2.1 In order to ensure randomness of selection, 
random number tables shall be used. For guidance and 
use of the random number tables reference may be 
made to IS 4905. In case these tables are not available, 
the following procedure is recommended for use: 


Starting from any one container, count them as 


where r is the integral part of N/n (N and n being the lot 
size and sample size respectively). Every r container 
thus counted shall be withdrawn to constitute the 
sample. 


D-2 PREPARATION OF TEST SAMPLES 


D-2.1 From each of the containers selected according 
to D-1.2.1, a representative portion of the material, 
sufficient to make triplicate determination for all the 
requirements given in 4, shall be drawn. 


11 


D-2.2 Out of these portions a small but approximately 
equal quantity of the material shall be taken and 
thoroughly mixed to form a composite sample, 
sufficient to carry out triplicate determination for all 
the characteristics tested on the composite sample. 
The composite sample shall be divided into three equal 
parts, one for the purchaser, another for the supplier 
and the third to be used as referee sample. 


D-2.3 The remaining portions of the material from each 
container shall be divided into three equal parts each 
forming an individual sample, one set of individual 
samples shall be marked for the purchaser, another for 
the supplier and the third to be used as a referee sample. 


D-2.4 All the individual and composite samples 
shall be transferred to separate containers. These 
containers shall be sealed air-tight and labelled with 
full identification particulars. 


D-2.5 The referee sample consisting of a composite 
sample and a set of individual samples shall bear the 
seals of both the purchaser and the supplier. They shall 
be kept at a place agreed to between the purchaser and 
the supplier to be used in case of any dispute between 
the two. 


D-3 NUMBER OF TESTS 


D-3.1 Tests for the determination of strength 
(see 4.2) and stability (see 4.3) of the material shall be 
conducted on each of the individual test samples and 
the test results shall be recorded separately for different 
test samples. 


D-3.2 Tests for the determination of all characteristics 
given in Table 1 shall be carried out on the composite 
test sample. 


D-4 CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY 


D-4.1 From the results recorded according to D-3.1 
the mean (X) and range (R) of test results for any 
characteristic shall be computed as follows: 

Sum of test result 1, 2,

minimum of the test results.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: CHD 01 (15804).
